description: An under-developed response that may or may not take a position. Typical elements:
typical element 1: Contains only general reasons with unelaborated and/or list-like details.
typical element 2: Shows little or no evidence of organization.
typical element 3: May be awkward and confused or simplistic.
typical element 4: May show little awareness of audience.

description: A minimally-developed response that may take a position, but with inadequate support and details
typical element 1: Has reasons with minimal elaboration and more general than specific details.
typical element 3: May be awkward in parts with few transitions.

description: A somewhat-developed response that takes a position and provides adequate support.
typical element 1: Has adequately elaborated reasons with a mix of general and specific details.
typical element 3: May be somewhat fluent with some transitional language.

description: A developed response that takes a clear position and provides reasonably persuasive support
typical element 1: Has moderately well elaborated reasons with mostly specific details.
typical element 3: May be moderately fluent with transitional language throughout.
typical element 4: May show a consistent awareness of audience.

description: A well-developed response that takes a clear and thoughtful position and provides persuasive support.
typical element 1: Has fully elaborated reasons with specific details.
typical element 3: Is fluent and uses sophisticated transitional language.
typical element 4: May show a heightened awareness of audience.
